info.title: Simple Host API
info.description:
Static website hosting with a light per-site backend. Deploy a site with one API call — inline JSON files (LLM-friendly) or a tar.gz/zip archive — and each site gets owner-declared KV, SQLite and file resources. Sign-in is a 6-digit email code or Google that returns an API key, sent as the `X-API-Key` header. Hosted-page sign-in uses the same account but a site-scoped session cookie on the site's own address — never an API key. Every site lives at its own address, `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/` (its own browser origin); `https://<handle>.simple-host.app/` lists the person's public sites. For a brand-new account a site may briefly live at `https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/` until its certificate is issued: use the `site_url` the API returns, never a composed one. Old `<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/` links redirect to the site's address, as do old `sites.simple-host.app/<handle>/<site>/` ones. Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code on the site's own address (a sign-in covers that site only). Owner-declared KV, SQLite and file resources use independent read/write policies including own reads and add-only writes; anonymous writes require an explicit write=anyone choice. Agents act as the owner with the API key (or connector) through `https://simple-host.app/v1/...`. Home-page, bio and showcase pin/order settings also work on small-box path installs: the public person page opens the selected site's existing URL. Hosted person hosts serve it at their root.  Whole-space custom domains have not shipped.
Older saved-data endpoints still work for sites that already use them; new sites use storage resources.

servers.description: Production API (agents, with an API key). Pages call the same /v1 routes same-origin on their own address.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Account sign-in by emailed code or Google, for Simple Host account owners and the agents working for them. It ends in an API key. It is never for a site's visitors: these routes answer only on the app's own address (403 account_auth_unavailable elsewhere), and an API key never belongs in a page. A page signs its visitors in with the Visitor sign-in routes through auth.js.

get.summary: Skills hub catalog — discover the bundled agent skills
get.description: Public catalog of the skills this server bundles (name + description + fetch URL), so any agent can search them over HTTP. No auth.

get.summary: Fetch one skill's SKILL.md (markdown)
get.description: Returns the raw SKILL.md for the named skill. Public, no auth.

get.summary: Fetch one skill's SKILL.md (markdown), same as /v1/skills/{name}
get.description: Same response as /v1/skills/{name}. Public, no auth.

get.summary: Fetch one of a skill's reference documents (markdown)
get.description: A skill's SKILL.md routes to reference documents under its references/ directory. A folder install has them on disk; install methods that fetch only SKILL.md by URL do not, so SKILL.md cites each reference by absolute URL as well and this endpoint serves it. Public, no auth.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The reference filename, e.g. backend.md

post.summary: Request an account sign-in code (account owners only)
post.description: For Simple Host account owners and their agents, never for a site's visitors. Answers only on the app's own address: on a site's address, a person's address, a connected domain, or from a page's origin it is 403 account_auth_unavailable, and no code is sent. A page signs its visitors in with POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/visitor/auth through auth.js instead. Emails a 6-digit code (and a magic link) to the address. No user row is created here — the account is created lazily on the first successful verify, so this can't be used to enumerate users.

nonce_hash.description: Browser pages only. base64url SHA-256 of a random nonce the page keeps. With it the email also carries a sign-in link, redeemable only together with that nonce (so only in that browser). Without it the email carries the code alone.

403.description: account_auth_unavailable: account sign-in answers only on the app's own address; a page's visitors use visitor sign-in (auth.js SH.mount).

post.summary: Verify the account code and get an API key (account owners only)
post.description: For Simple Host account owners and their agents, never for a site's visitors. Answers only on the app's own address (403 account_auth_unavailable elsewhere), so no site page can mint an account key. A page signs its visitors in with POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/visitor/auth/verify through auth.js, which sets a cookie for that one site and never returns a key. Exchange `{email, code}` (CLI/agent) or a magic-link `{token}` (browser) for an API key. The first successful email-code verify creates the account. Dashboard Google also redeems through this endpoint (`/?token=&cn=`). A link token is redeemed only with the `nonce` whose hash it was issued with, so a sign-in link works only in the browser that asked for it. Visitor-issued codes are not accepted here. The code expires in 15 minutes and allows 3 attempts.

nonce.description: required with token — the nonce whose hash was sent when the link was requested

name.description: Optional label for the key this sign-in issues, shown in the Keys list (GET /v1/me/keys). Defaults to "dashboard sign-in" for a link or Google, "agent sign-in" for a typed code.

choose_handle.description: When this sign-in would create a new account: create nothing yet and answer 409 with code choose_handle and a suggested_handle, without using up the code. Ask the person which address they want, then verify again with the same code and handle. Ignored for an existing account.

handle.description: The address (<handle>.simple-host.app) a NEW account takes; ignored for an existing account. Refused as 400 invalid_handle, 409 handle_reserved or 409 handle_taken without using up the code, so another can be tried. It can be changed later (PATCH /v1/me), not more than once in 30 days after publishing. Without handle or choose_handle a new account is given one.

403.description: account_auth_unavailable: account sign-in answers only on the app's own address; a page's visitors use visitor sign-in (auth.js SH.mount).

409.description: code choose_handle (a new account: choose its address first; carries suggested_handle and address), or handle_taken / handle_reserved (the handle sent cannot be had; error names the address). The code is not used up.

401.description: Invalid or expired code

get.summary: Is this address (handle) free?
get.description: Whether <handle>.simple-host.app can be taken as an account's address: at sign-up (POST /v1/auth/verify with handle) or as a change (PATCH /v1/me). Handles, old handles that still redirect, free <name>.simple-host.app addresses claimed by sites, other accounts' live site names (an unclaimed <name>.simple-host.app still redirects to that site) and reserved names share one namespace. With X-API-Key the account's own handle counts as available. Rate limited per address (RATE_LIMIT_HANDLE_CHECK); no CORS, and a cross-site browser request gets 403. A claim still decides.

error.example: That address is taken: rose.simple-host.app is already in use. Try another.

429.description: Too many checks from this address

get.summary: List enabled sign-in methods (public discovery)
get.description: Public discovery for pages and the dashboard: auth.js reads it from a site to offer Google; it is not account sign-in and sets nothing. Google (more providers later). Returns the enabled provider names (`google`) so pages never hardcode a provider. Empty when sign-in is not configured. Sign-in creates or links a `users` row; a hosted-page session still does not disclose an API key.

email_enabled.description: Whether email sign-in codes are configured

get.summary: Start account Google sign-in (account owners; a site sign-in is forwarded)
get.description: Account sign-in starts only on the app's own address. On any other host (a site's address, a connected domain) the same path answers 302 to GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider} on that host with the same return_to, so a hand-written link still reaches visitor sign-in and never an account key; from a page's origin on the apex it is 403 account_auth_unavailable. A page offers Google to its visitors with auth.js SH.signIn(), which starts at GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider} on the site's own host. Apex start. Query `return_to` is required and must be an absolute URL. Two shapes: the dashboard origin `/` (owner purpose — callback hands off via `/?token=`; success 302s to the provider with PKCE S256) or a site's own address — a site host `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/...` (or, while that person's certificate is pending, the person address `https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/...`), a claimed name or a DNS-proven bound domain (site purpose). A site-purpose start is not begun here: it 302s to `GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider}` on that site's own host, which binds the sign-in to the browser. Unknown or disabled provider is 404. No cookie is set here. The Legacy path-address (`sites.<domain>/<handle>/<site>/`) return_to URLs are rejected with 400 invalid return_to, as are apex URLs outside the dashboard. The caller cannot set `purpose`; it is derived from `return_to`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Absolute URL of the page to return to after sign-in

403.description: account_auth_unavailable: on the app's address but from a page's origin.

get.summary: OAuth callback (apex only)
get.description: Answers only on the app's own address (403 account_auth_unavailable elsewhere). Provider redirect URI on the apex. Consumes the one-time `state`. Identifies via userinfo, then `resolveUser` (link or create a `users` row on a verified email; refuse missing/unverified email). Site purpose 302s to `https://<return-host>/v1/visitor/establish?once=…`. Owner purpose 302s to `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/?token=…` for the dashboard to redeem via `POST /v1/auth/verify`. Neither redirect contains an API key. Failures are a short no-store HTML page on the apex with no Location and no cookie.

403.description: account_auth_unavailable: not on the app's own address.

302.description: Site purpose: redirect to /v1/visitor/establish on the stored host. Owner purpose: redirect to /?token= on PUBLIC_BASE_URL.

400.description: Bad, replayed, or expired state, or provider error

get.summary: Start visitor sign-in on the site's own host
get.description: Visitor sign-in start, served on the site's own address (its `<site>.<handle>` host, person address, claimed name or bound domain). `return_to` must be a page on this same host that belongs to the site served here. Sets a short-lived host-only nonce cookie (`__Host-sh_vnonce`, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 10 minutes; `sh_vnonce` on local HTTP), stores only its SHA-256 with the OAuth state, and 302s to the provider with PKCE S256. `GET /v1/visitor/establish` later sets the session only in the browser holding that nonce, so a sign-in finished elsewhere cannot be completed in another browser (login CSRF). auth.js `SH.signIn()` navigates here.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Absolute URL of a page on this host to return to after sign-in

302.description: Nonce cookie set; redirect to the identity provider

400.description: Missing return_to, or one that is not a page of the site on this host

get.summary: Establish the visitor session cookie
get.description: One-time hop on the site's own address (its `<site>.<handle>` host or domain). Consumes `once`, host-matches, requires the `__Host-sh_vnonce` cookie set by `GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider}` in this browser (its hash must match the one bound to the code; the code is burned on any failure), sets `__Host-sh_vsess` (or `sh_vsess` on local HTTP), clears the nonce cookie, then 302s to the stored `return_to` with no query mutation. Never sets a cookie on the apex or the legacy path address. Failures are HTML, no cookie, no redirect.

302.description: Cookie set; redirect to the stored return_to

400.description: Bad, replayed, expired, host-mismatch, missing or wrong nonce cookie, or apex Host

post.summary: Log out this visitor session
post.description: Deletes the session named by the visitor cookie and clears the cookie. Requires `X-SH-CSRF: 1` or `Content-Type: application/json` (not a simple form post).

403.description: Missing CSRF header (and not a JSON request)

patch.summary: Edit display name or change your handle
patch.description: Changing the handle changes every address (https://<handle>.simple-host.app/ and https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/). Before anything is published it changes freely. After that (even once every site is gone) it can change once every 30 days: the old handle stays reserved for this account and every old address redirects to the new one. A new handle gets its own certificate; until it is issued, sites briefly use the fallback https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/. What pages kept in visitors' browsers starts empty at the new address, and visitors sign in again.

display_name.description: Trimmed; empty clears the name. Never used in URLs.

handle.description: The <handle> in your address https://<handle>.simple-host.app/. Must not be reserved or already taken (handles and free <name>.simple-host.app addresses share one namespace).

signin_alerts.description: Sign-in alert emails (default true): one email after each sign-in or app connection, at most one per browser or app a day. Needs one of the account's own API keys (a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key).

400.description: Invalid profile, or signin_alerts sent without an account key (code not_an_account_key)

401.description: API key required

409.description: The handle cannot be had: code handle_taken (another account's handle or old handle, or a site's claimed free name; error says "That address is taken: <handle>.simple-host.app is already in use. Try another.") or handle_reserved. A malformed handle is 400 invalid_handle.

429.description: The handle already changed within the last 30 days after publishing

get.summary: Current user

handle.description: The <handle> in your addresses: sites at https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/, your page at https://<handle>.simple-host.app/

home_site.description: Chosen home site name; null means showcase. Rename follows the site, deletion clears it.

public_page.description: The account's public page listing its public sites, e.g. https://<handle>.simple-host.app/. Present with handle.

signin_alerts.description: Whether an email follows each sign-in or app connection (PATCH /v1/me to change).

max_sites.description: Sites this account may hold (sites in Recently deleted count; one more is 403 site_quota_reached): the instance's MAX_SITES_PER_ACCOUNT, or the account's own MAX_SITES_OVERRIDES entry. Absent for admins, who have no limit.

file_usage.description: Website files and kept versions including the live copy and Recently deleted sites; saved data and storage resources excluded

can_set_keep_versions.description: Account is allowed to change per-site retention

max_site_mb.description: Largest site this account may deploy, in MB (an upload or its unpacked files over it is 413 site_too_large): the instance's MAX_ARCHIVE_MB, or the account's own MAX_ARCHIVE_MB_OVERRIDES entry. A site already larger stays up.

delete.summary: Delete your account and all its data
delete.description: Deletes the account at once and for good; nothing goes to Recently deleted and nothing can be restored. Removed: every site (including ones in Recently deleted) with its files, versions, saved data, lists and analytics; keys; connected apps; visitor sign-ins; and every entry this person sent to other people's lists while signed in; their address is taken off the changes they made to other people's page data (writes made without signing in and older public-list entries are not linked to anyone and stay; support@simple-host.app helps with those). The handle, old handles and claimed <name>.simple-host.app addresses are retired, never given to anyone else; custom domains are released. A confirmation email goes to the account's address. Offer GET /v1/me/export.zip first. Refused for a suspended account or one holding a site the operator took down (the operator handles those), an admin account, or one still holding event hostnames.

confirm.description: The account's handle, or its email when it has no handle. Case-insensitive.

400.description: confirm missing (code confirm_required) or does not match (code confirm_mismatch)

403.description: Suspended account (code account_suspended), a site of the account taken down (code site_suspended) or admin account (code admin_account)

409.description: The account still holds event hostnames (code event_hostnames)

429.description: Too many requests from this address

post.summary: Change your sign-in email, step 1: send codes to the new and the current address
post.description: Emails a 6-digit code to the new address and another to the current one (15 minutes, 3 tries). Send both to POST /v1/me/email/verify to finish. Asking looks the same for every address. Needs one of the account's own API keys: a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key. Refused for the plugin reviewer account (and for moving any account to its address), admin, event and preview accounts, and accounts whose sign-in name is not an email address. Rate-limited per address and per account, like sign-in.

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key), not an email (code invalid_email), already the sign-in email (code same_email), or the reviewer's address (code reserved_email)

403.description: The reviewer, an admin, event or preview account, or one with no email to confirm from (codes reviewer_account, admin_account, event_account, preview_account, no_current_email)

post.summary: Change your sign-in email, step 2: confirm with both codes
post.description: Moves the account to the new address: from now on sign-in codes go there. The handle, sites and connected apps stay; every other API key of the account is signed out (the one making the call stays); linked Google/GitHub sign-ins stay (GET /v1/me/identities lists them). Open sign-in codes for the old address stop working, the account's emailed idle-site links end, and the old address gets a notice naming the new one masked (n***@example.com) with an undo link valid for 7 days. An address another account signs in with is refused here, after the codes are verified (409 email_taken). Needs one of the account's own API keys.

code.description: The 6-digit code emailed to the new address

current_code.description: The 6-digit code emailed to the current address

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key), a code missing (code codes_required), no change waiting (code no_pending_change), or the reviewer's address (code reserved_email)

401.description: Wrong or expired code, or too many tries (code invalid_code)

403.description: The reviewer, an admin, event or preview account (see step 1)

409.description: Another account signs in with that address (code email_taken)

get.summary: "This wasn't me" link from the old address's notice (confirmation page)
get.description: Shows a page with an Undo button and changes nothing. No sign-in; the token is the authorization. 404 page when the link was used or is older than 7 days. Emailed links carry the token in the fragment (`#t=`), so it never reaches a server log: without `t` the GET returns a small page whose script posts the fragment's token back with `peek=1`, which shows this confirmation. Links sent before v0.7.1 carry `?t=` and keep working until they expire.

200.description: HTML confirmation page with the button

404.description: HTML page; the link was used or has expired

post.summary: Undo a sign-in email change
post.description: The confirmation page's button (with `peek=1`, only the confirmation page). Puts the account back on the old address, signs out every API key and every sign-in on sites, removes Google/GitHub sign-ins and connected apps added since the change, and spends every undo link of the account. HTML page.

200.description: HTML page; the account signs in with the old address again

404.description: HTML page; the link was used or has expired

409.description: HTML page; another account signs in with the old address now

get.summary: Google and GitHub accounts that sign in to yours
get.description: Own API key only (400 not_an_account_key otherwise).

delete.summary: Unlink a Google or GitHub sign-in
delete.description: That Google or GitHub account no longer signs in to yours. Own API key only.

404.description: No such sign-in on this account

get.summary: Download all your data (one .zip)
get.description: Streams one .zip of everything held about the account: README.txt; account.json (email, handle, display name, created, earlier handles, claimed names including retired ones, custom domains, linked Google/GitHub sign-ins); keys.json (name, last 4 characters, created, last used; never keys or hashes); connected_apps.json (name, connected, last used); visitor.json (sites signed in to as a visitor with first sign-in and last seen, every entry sent to other people's lists while signed in, and `changed`: every change made to other people's page data or list entries while signed in, as site, what, change and when); sites/<name>/ for every live site in the same layout as GET /v1/sites/{sitename}/export.tar.gz (files/, state.json, collections.json); and recently-deleted/<name>/ for every site in Recently deleted, in the same layout plus deleted.json (deleted_at, removed_for_good_at). Visitor analytics hold no personal data (salted hashes) and are not included. Needs one of the account's own API keys: a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key. A suspended account gets 403 account_suspended and writes to support@simple-host.app for a copy of its data.

400.description: Not one of the account's own API keys (code not_an_account_key)

403.description: The account is suspended (code account_suspended); write to support@simple-host.app for a copy of the data

get.summary: Download all your data (older address)
get.description: The address Download my data had before it became a .zip. Serves exactly what GET /v1/me/export.zip serves: the same .zip, with Content-Type application/zip and a .zip filename, under the same rules. Use /v1/me/export.zip.

400.description: Not one of the account's own API keys (code not_an_account_key)

post.summary: Sign out everywhere (rotate your API key)
post.description: The "Sign out everywhere" button. Replaces all of the authenticated owner's API keys with one new key and returns it. Every older key stops working immediately, and every connected app (see /v1/me/connections) is disconnected. Keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, so this response is the only time the new key is shown.

get.summary: List connected apps
get.description: The AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, a GPT Action) this account has connected through the Simple Host connector (OAuth at /oauth/authorize, MCP at /mcp). Each is listed once, however many times it was connected.

name.description: The name the app registered with

device.description: The browser the connection was approved on, summarised, to tell two connections of the same app apart. Never the user agent itself or an IP. Empty when unknown (and for connections made before 2026-09-27).

get.summary: List recently deleted sites
get.description: Sites this account deleted in the last 7 days. Each keeps its files, versions, saved data, collections and addresses, and its name stays taken, until purge_at; POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/restore brings it back until then.

200.description: Recently deleted sites, most recently deleted first

purge_at.description: When it is removed for good

delete.summary: Disconnect an app
delete.description: Revokes every token this account granted to the app. It has to be connected again, with a fresh sign-in, to be used.

404.description: No connected app with that id

post.summary: Sign out (end the key this request used)
post.description: Deletes the API key sent with this request, so it stops working everywhere; the account's other keys and connected apps are untouched. The dashboard's Sign out calls this before it clears the key from the browser. Needs one of the account's own keys (the admin env key or a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key).

204.description: Signed out; the key no longer works

400.description: Not one of the account's own keys (code not_an_account_key)

get.summary: List your API keys
get.description: Every key on the account, newest first. `current` marks the key this request was made with. Keys issued before names existed have no `name` or `last4` (shown as "Earlier key"). `last_used_at` is updated at most every 5 minutes. A key unused for 180 days stops working. `idle_expires_at` says when (KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS); one minted with `expires_in_days` stops at `expires_at`. A key that has stopped stays listed with `expired` until revoked.

post.summary: Create a named API key
post.description: Mints a new key with the given name (for a CI secret or another machine) and returns it once; it is stored only as a hash. `scope: deploy` makes a deploy-only key: it may create, update, roll back and list sites, read their versions and files, and make preview links; every other route (delete, rename, domains, keys, saved data and lists, analytics, the account, connecting apps, and the same through /mcp) answers 403 deploy_only_key. Use it for a CI secret. `expires_in_days` (1-3650) gives the key a fixed expiry; without it the key stops only when it goes unused (KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS). Needs one of the account's own keys (the admin env key or a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key). An account holds at most 50 keys (409 key_limit; keys that have stopped working do not count, and are deleted 30 days after they stop). A deploy key never carries admin powers. A deploy key can publish code that runs when you open your own site (signed in there, that code acts with your powers over its saved data); treat it like the site itself; a key revoked or rotated away mid-request gets 401 invalid_api_key.

name.description: Any label except the names Simple Host gives its own keys (dashboard sign-in, agent sign-in, event account, reviewer sign-in, replacement key; 400)

scope.description: deploy: create, update, roll back and list sites and make preview links, nothing else

expires_in_days.description: Optional fixed expiry, in days from now

201.description: Key created. `api_key` is shown only here.

409.description: The account already holds 50 keys (code key_limit); revoke one first.

delete.summary: Revoke one API key
delete.description: The key stops working at once; the account's other keys and connected apps are untouched. Revoking the key this request uses signs this caller out. Needs one of the account's own keys.

400.description: Not one of the account's own keys (code not_an_account_key)

404.description: No key with that id on this account

get.summary: List your sites
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's sites. Admins see all sites. On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

post.summary: Deploy a site from inline JSON files
post.description: The LLM-friendly deploy path — send every file inline in one request, no archiving. Text goes in `files`; base64-encoded binary goes in `files_base64`. `index.html` is required. Relative paths only (`..`/absolute are rejected); secret files (`.env`, `.git/*`, `id_rsa`) are dropped and script extensions (`.sh .py .php …`) are rejected. Use PUT to update an existing site (409 site_exists says so); PUT with ?create=1 creates or updates in one call. On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

put.summary: Update a site from inline JSON files
put.description: Same as POST, but for an existing site you own. Creates a new version and activates it; with ?publish=false the version is only stored (visitors keep seeing the live one) and the answer adds unpublished_version, preview_url and preview_expires_at. With ?create=1 a missing site is created instead (201, with the same checks as POST), so CI deploys in one call; without it a missing site is 404. On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

201.description: Site created (?create=1 and no site of that name)

patch.summary: Rename your site, or take it offline
patch.description: One change per request. With {"offline": true} the site is taken offline: every address answers a plain "This site is offline" page (503), and visitor saves (state and collection writes from a page, private lists included), visitors' reads of its state and lists, and visitor sign-in are refused with 403 site_offline; files, versions and saved data are kept, and the owner's key or connector still deploys, reads and writes. {"offline": false} puts it back online. An operator take-down wins over it, and a taken-down site cannot be switched (403 site_suspended). The answer is the site object with `offline` and a `note`. With {"name": "new-name"} it renames the database row and on-disk site directory. The new name uses the same validation and per-owner uniqueness rule as creation. A bound custom domain remains attached. Links to the old name keep working: its site host, person-path and sites.* addresses 302 to the new address (path and query kept), through any chain of renames, until a site with the old name is created again (the new site wins); the response says so with old_url_status "redirects". Deleting the site stops the redirects (restoring brings them back); purging it removes them.

schema.description: Exactly one of name or offline.

offline.description: true takes the site offline; false puts it back online.

200.description: Renamed (old_name, name, old_url, site_url, old_url_status) or switched (the site object with offline and note)

403.description: The operator has taken the site down (code site_suspended)

post.summary: Create a site from an archive
post.description: Upload a `.tar.gz` or `.zip` (for framework builds, binary assets, large sites). Max 100 MB. On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

put.summary: Update a site from an archive
put.description: Upload a new version of an existing site you own. Creates a new version and activates it; with ?publish=false the version is only stored (visitors keep seeing the live one) and the answer adds unpublished_version, preview_url and preview_expires_at. With ?create=1 a missing site is created instead (201, with the same checks as POST): one call from CI, e.g. `curl -X PUT ".../v1/sites/<name>?create=1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" --data-binary @site.tar.gz`. On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

201.description: Site created (?create=1 and no site of that name)

delete.summary: Delete your site
delete.description: Takes the site offline at once, with every version, its saved state and collections. It stays in Recently deleted (GET /v1/me/deleted-sites) for 7 days with its name held, and POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/restore brings it back exactly as it was; after that it is removed for good. Creating a site with a held name answers 409 with recently_deleted true.

post.summary: Restore a recently deleted site
post.description: Brings a site back from Recently deleted under the same name and address, with every version, its saved data, collections and connected address, live at once.

404.description: No site with that name in Recently deleted

get.summary: Download a site as a tar.gz
get.description: Streams the site's published files (`files/`), its saved JSON state (`state.json`) and its collections (`collections.json`: every list, private ones included, each entry as `{id, created_at, submitted_by, data}`; `submitted_by` only on private lists) as one archive. Exists because an event instance is destroyed when the event ends and nothing is backed up, so the person who built something can take it with them. The saved data comes first: the files usually exist somewhere else, the JSON only lives here.

post.summary: Make a 10-minute download link for a site's export
post.description: Returns a link that downloads the same archive as `export.tar.gz` without an API key, for people who use Simple Host only through a chat app's connector (the `export_site` tool). The link is signed for this owner and this site, expires after 10 minutes, and stops working if the site is deleted or the server restarts. Anyone holding it can download the copy until then, so hand it to the person only.

get.summary: Download a site's export through a link from export-link
get.description: No API key: the signed `token` is the whole authorization, for one site, for 10 minutes. Streams the archive described under `export.tar.gz`. An expired, altered or unknown token, or one for a site since deleted or moved to another account, answers 404 with code `export_link_invalid`.

404.description: The link is not valid or has expired

example.error: this download link is not valid or has expired

get.summary: List a site's versions
get.description: The versions this instance still holds, newest first. An instance may be configured to keep only the last few deploys, or only the live one, in which case older versions are absent here and from disk. KEEP_VERSIONS controls it; event boxes are installed with 1.

status.description: active: complete and live now or before; ready: stored with publish=false and never live yet

get.summary: List files in a retained version
get.description: Owner only. Walks the version directory; paths are relative, use forward slashes, and are sorted. Pruned versions return 404.

404.description: Site not found or version not found (including pruned versions)

get.summary: Read a file from a retained version
get.description: Owner only. Streams raw bytes with a Content-Type based on the file extension (application/octet-stream fallback; HTML uses UTF-8). Directories return 404. Paths containing '..', leading slashes, backslashes, NUL, or symlinks escaping the version directory are rejected. Pruned versions return 404.

post.summary: Preview a kept version
post.description: Owner only. Mints a link, working for anyone who has it for one hour, that shows one kept version (live, earlier, or stored with publish=false) exactly as visitors would see it, on the site's own host: https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/__preview/<n>/<token>/ (or briefly, as a fallback while the person's certificate is not ready, <handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/__preview/...). The token is an HMAC over site, version and expiry; it stops working after an hour or a server restart. Preview pages are noindex and never cached, and saves made from them are refused (403 preview_read_only; told apart by the Referer, so a page that suppresses its Referer is not stopped: this guards against accidents, and the pages are the owner's own). Make the version live with PUT .../active-version.

live.description: Whether visitors see this version now

403.description: The operator has taken the site down (code site_suspended)

404.description: Site or version not found (including pruned versions)

409.description: No preview link (code preview_unavailable): the site has no address of its own yet, or the server gives sites none (every site on one shared address, as on a small box), which the message says

put.summary: Roll back to a version, or make a stored version live
put.description: Re-point the live site at an existing version number: an earlier one, or one stored with publish=false (which then counts as live). On simple-hack.app (EVENTS=hosted) only a team key (or a connector bound to a team) deploys, to its own team's site only; errors 403 no_personal_sites, 403 team_site_only, 403 team_key_scope, 401 team_key_inactive, 409 team_sites_not_ready, 409 submissions_closed, 403 team_site_taken_down.

put.summary: Set showcase visibility
put.description:
Set whether this site is listed on the owner's account page at https://<handle>.simple-host.app/. `public` = listed there; `unlisted` = hidden from it. New sites are created `unlisted` — listing is an explicit act, not a side effect of deploying.

This controls LISTING ONLY. Both values are equally reachable by anyone with the URL; nothing on the content-serving path consults it. `unlisted` is not privacy and must never be described as such. Owner only (API key).

put.summary: Keep a site up for good
put.description: Mark the site Keep (or clear the mark). Where the idle-site cleanup is on (simple-host.app), a site with no visits by people and no new version for 90 days gets its owner an email with a "Keep it" link (and a link to their page, where they can sign in and download it); 30 days later with nothing done it moves to Recently deleted (restorable for 7 days, with a link in a second email). A site marked Keep is never flagged, and marking it ends a pending warning. Sites with their own domain or claimed name are never flagged either. Owner only (API key).

423.description: The site is taken down by the operator

put.summary: Set how many versions of a site are kept
put.description: Every deploy stores a full copy of the site as a new version. keep_versions sets how many this site keeps: N from 1 to 1000 keeps the newest N plus any older live version. 0 goes back to the account default (KEEP_VERSIONS_OVERRIDES), else this server's setting (KEEP_VERSIONS; 0 there means keep every version). Setting it removes the older versions at once, for good (their files and their rows; removed_versions names them), and every later deploy removes whatever falls outside it. The value is on the site (keep_versions in GET /v1/sites) when set. Owner only (a full API key; a deploy-only key is refused, since this deletes history). Only accounts in KEEP_VERSIONS_SELF_SET (current or old handles) may set a count when that knob is set. Others get 403 keep_versions_fixed with the plain message "Simple Host keeps your 4 latest versions". Hosted defaults: 4; the chhotabreak, vineetu and jot-transcribe exceptions default to 10.

200.description: The setting as stored, and what it removed

keep_versions.description: The site's own setting; 0 = this server's

effective_keep_versions.description: What applies to this site now; 0 = every version is kept

removed_versions.description: Version numbers removed by this call (empty when none)

400.description: Body is not {"keep_versions": N} with N from 0 to 1000

403.description: A deploy-only key (deploy_only_key), or an account whose version count is fixed (keep_versions_fixed)

423.description: The site is taken down by the operator

429.description: Too many site changes from this address; try again shortly

get.summary: Whether a site has a passcode, and the passcode
get.description: Owner only (the owner's key or connector token; a deploy-only key is refused). Says whether the site asks visitors for a passcode and, when it does, the passcode itself and when it was set. The passcode is stored sealed with a server key (AES-256-GCM under PASSCODE_ENC_KEY), so the owner can read it back; the admin's routes never read it. If the server's key changed, `passcode` is absent and `note` says to set a new one. Never cached (Cache-Control: no-store).

put.summary: Put a passcode on a whole site, or change it
put.description: Owner only (the owner's key or connector token; a deploy-only key is refused). Every address of the site (its own address, the person path while its certificate is pending, a free name, a custom domain) then answers a plain "This site is protected" page (401, noindex, no-store; nothing of the site in it; robots.txt answers `Disallow: /`) until the visitor enters the passcode. A right passcode sets an unlock cookie for that one host (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, `__Host-` prefixed, about 400 days) that lasts until the passcode changes or the owner signs everyone out; `.app` and `.site` addresses each need their own unlock. Send `{"passcode": "..."}` (any characters, at least PASSCODE_MIN_LENGTH, default 6, at most 128; digits only is fine; spaces around it are trimmed) or `{"generate": true}` for 6 random digits. Setting the same passcode again changes nothing; a different one signs everyone out. The site leaves the person page. The owner's key, connector token and the admin key still read and write its data; previews still open. Take-down (410) and offline (503) win over the passcode. There is no end date: take the site offline or delete it instead. A passcode keeps out people who don't have it: search engines, link previews, and anyone who finds or is forwarded the link without it. Anyone given it can open the site and pass it on. It is not a login, it does not say who visited, and it does not make saved data private per person.

schema.description: Exactly one of passcode or generate

generate.description: true: the server picks 6 random digits

200.description: The passcode is set (the answer carries it)

400.description: Body is not {"passcode": "..."} or {"generate": true} (invalid_request), or the passcode is too short or too long (invalid_passcode)

403.description: The operator has taken the site down (site_suspended), or a deploy-only key (deploy_only_key)

409.description: passcodes_not_enabled (SITE_PASSCODES is off or PASSCODE_ENC_KEY is unset on this server), or passcode_needs_own_address (every site on this server shares one address, as on a small box or an event box, so an unlock would cover every site)

delete.summary: Remove a site's passcode
delete.description: Owner only (the owner's key or connector token; a deploy-only key is refused). Every address of the site opens to everyone again. Removing a passcode the site does not have is not an error.

post.summary: Sign every visitor out of a site with a passcode
post.description: Owner only (the owner's key or connector token; a deploy-only key is refused). Ends every unlock at once, on every address: each visitor must enter the passcode again. The passcode stays the same.

get.summary: Who can open a site, and its named viewers
get.description: Owner only (the owner's key or connector token; a deploy-only key is refused). `access` is `anyone` (anyone with the address, or with the passcode when the site has one) or `specific` (only the owner and the named viewers, each signed in with visitor sign-in on the site's own address). `viewers` lists the named viewers by the email they sign in with. Never cached (Cache-Control: no-store). Hosted Simple Host and small boxes only; not on Simple Hack.

put.summary: Choose who can open a site (anyone, or only named viewers)
put.description: Owner only. `{"access": "specific"}`: every address of the site (its own address, a custom domain, a free name, an address family, the person address when it is the home page) then shows a sign-in page (401, noindex, no-store, nothing of the site in it) to anyone not signed in on that address, and a plain "This site is private" page (403) with Switch account and Sign out to someone signed in who is not the owner or a named viewer. The site's saved data (state, collections, storage resources, whatever their site_passcode says) answers 403 `site_private` to them too; the owner's key and connector keep working, and previews still open. With no viewers named only the owner can open it. `{"access": "anyone"}` opens it again and keeps the list. The site leaves the person page while it is specific. A site has named viewers or a passcode, never both (409 passcode_set). Every request is checked against the list as it is then: a removed person is refused on their next request.

200.description: Who can open the site now, with a plain `note`

403.description: The operator has taken the site down (site_suspended), or a deploy-only key (deploy_only_key)

409.description: passcode_set (remove the passcode first), named_viewers_need_own_address (every site on this server shares one address), sign_in_unavailable (this server has no email codes or Google), or named_viewers_unavailable (Simple Hack)

post.summary: Name viewers by email, and open the site only to them
post.description: Owner only. Adds each email (trimmed and lower-cased; letters, digits and `._%+-` before the `@`; matched exactly, with no folding of dots or `+tags`) to the site's named viewers and sets access to `specific` in the same call. At most SITE_VIEWERS_MAX (default 50) per site. `added` lists the new ones, `already_listed` the ones that were there.

200.description: Who can open the site now

400.description: invalid_request, invalid_email (names the address), or too_many_viewers (more than SITE_VIEWERS_MAX in one call)

409.description: too_many_viewers (the list would pass SITE_VIEWERS_MAX), passcode_set, named_viewers_need_own_address, sign_in_unavailable or named_viewers_unavailable

delete.summary: Remove one named viewer
delete.description: Owner only. The person's next request is refused. Access does not change: removing the last viewer leaves the site open only to its owner.

200.description: Who can open the site now (`removed` names the email)

404.description: No such site, or the email is not a named viewer (viewer_not_found)

post.summary: Enter a site's passcode (the "This site is protected" form)
post.description: The form on the "This site is protected" page posts here, on the site's own host; no key. The site is the one the host names (on a person host, the first path segment of `next`). Only a form from a page on the same host is accepted (another origin gets 403 origin_not_allowed as JSON). A right passcode answers 303 to `next` with the unlock cookie for this host. A wrong one answers the gate page again (401). Wrong tries are limited per site and address (RATE_LIMIT_PASSCODE_IP, default 5 per 3 minutes, then PASSCODE_LOCKOUT_MINUTES, default 15) and per site from everyone together (RATE_LIMIT_PASSCODE_SITE, default 60 a minute, then PASSCODE_SITE_LOCKOUT_MINUTES, default 15, when every try is refused; visitors already let in are not affected): 429 with Retry-After.

next.description: A path on this host to return to (default /)

Set-Cookie.description: The unlock cookie: __Host-sh_pass_<id>, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, about 400 days

401.description: Wrong passcode: the gate page again, saying so (text/html, noindex, no-store)

429.description: Too many wrong tries: the gate page saying when to try again (text/html)

post.summary: Sign in from a named-viewers site's sign-in page
post.description: The form on a named-viewers site's sign-in page posts here, on the site's own host; no key, no JavaScript. With `email` alone it sends a sign-in code (to any address, listed or not, so the form never says who is on the list) and answers the code page (401, text/html). With `email` and `code` it signs the visitor in to this site on this host (the same visitor session as auth.js) and answers 303 to `next`. Only a form from a page on the same host is accepted (403 origin_not_allowed otherwise). On a site that is not specific it answers 303 to `next`. Rate limited per address and per email like visitor sign-in.

next.description: A path on this host to return to (default /)

Set-Cookie.description: The visitor session cookie __Host-sh_vsess for this host

401.description: The code page, or the sign-in page again with the reason (text/html, noindex, no-store)

post.summary: Sign out from a named-viewers site's private page
post.description: The Switch account and Sign out buttons on "This site is private" post here, on the site's own host. Ends this host's visitor session and answers 303 to `next`, which then shows the sign-in page. Only a form from a page on the same host is accepted.

get.summary: "Keep it" link from an idle-site email (confirmation page)
get.description: Opened from the idle-site email; no sign-in, the token is the authorization. Shows a page with a "Keep it online" button and changes nothing (mail scanners follow links). 404 page when the link was used, replaced or has expired; 403 page while the site is taken down. Emailed links carry the token in the fragment (`#t=`), so it never reaches a server log: without `t` the GET returns a small page whose script posts the fragment's token back with `peek=1`, which shows this confirmation. Links sent before v0.7.1 carry `?t=` and keep working until they expire.

Emailed links carry the token in the fragment (`#t=`), so it never reaches a server log: without `t` the GET returns a small page whose script posts the fragment's token back with `peek=1`, which shows this confirmation. Links sent before v0.7.1 carry `?t=` and keep working until they expire.

get.summary: Per-site traffic totals for every site you own
get.description:
One call returning the class split for all of the caller's sites, ordered by `person.views` descending — the "which of my sites are actually being read" view. Exists so a dashboard can sort by traffic without one request per site.

Not under `/v1/sites/...` because that would collide with a site named "analytics". Pass `all=1` (admins only) to widen the scope to every site on the instance; non-admins get 403 rather than a silently narrowed list.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of UTC days to include (default 30, clamp 1..365)

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Admins only — include every site on the instance.

get.summary: Get per-site visitor analytics
get.description:
Owner-scoped view and visitor counts derived server-side from the access log (no client beacon). Every bucket is split three ways by who was asking: `person` (no automation signature), `bot` (crawlers, AI scrapers, SEO tools, security scanners, HTTP libraries) and `infra` (uptime probes and health checks aimed at the site). Read `person` as the audience number — a total that folds in `infra` is dominated by monitoring, not people.

`visitors` are unique visitors: COUNT(DISTINCT hashed IP) over the window asked for. The salt is stable, so `totals.*.visitors` is genuine uniques for the range and is NOT the sum of the `daily` figures — someone who visited on five days is one unique in `totals` and five in `daily`. IP-based, so a shared office NAT reads as one visitor and a phone switching wifi→cellular reads as two.

`daily` is zero-filled dense for the requested window (oldest → newest). `hourly` is always 24 zero-filled buckets ending with the hour in progress. Only successful document responses (200/304, non-asset paths) count as views, for every class alike. Owner only (API key).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of UTC days to include (default 30, clamp 1..365)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle of the account that owns the site. Omit it (or pass your own handle) for your own site. Any other handle is honoured for the platform admin only; for everyone else it answers 404, the same as a site that does not exist.

classified_from.description: First UTC day for which the person/bot/infra split exists. Earlier days in `daily` report under `unknown`. Omitted when nothing has been classified yet.

get.summary: Where a site's visitors are, by country
get.description:
Per-country traffic for one site over the last `days` UTC days, split by the same `person` / `bot` / `infra` classes as the rest of analytics and ordered by `person.views` descending (ties broken by country code).

Country is resolved on the server from a local IP-range table refreshed from a public dataset — no visitor address is ever sent to a geolocation service, and the raw address is still never stored. Country data: "IP Geolocation by DB-IP" (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

`country` is ISO-3166 alpha-2. `"XX"` / `"Unknown"` is traffic the table could not place (an unlisted block, or a server whose ranges have not been loaded); it is listed rather than dropped, so the countries still add up to the site's totals.

`visitors` is COUNT(DISTINCT hashed IP) over the whole window, exactly as in the main analytics endpoint — genuine uniques for the range, not the sum of the daily figures. Someone whose address changes country mid-range counts once in each, so the columns can total slightly more than the site's own figure. `unknown` is always zero here: the pre-classifier history has no addresses left to place. Owner only (API key).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of UTC days to include (default 30, clamp 1..365)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle of the account that owns the site. Omit it (or pass your own handle) for your own site. Any other handle is honoured for the platform admin only; for everyone else it answers 404, the same as a site that does not exist.

200.description: Per-country traffic, most real people first.

get.summary: A site's top pages and where its visitors came from
get.description: The 20 most viewed pages (path on the site, without the query string or fragment, percent-escapes decoded once and `//` collapsed) and the 20 top referring domains over the last `days` UTC days, people only, most views first. A site keeps at most ANALYTICS_PAGES_PER_SITE_DAY pages and ANALYTICS_REFERRERS_PER_SITE_DAY domains a day; the views of further new ones that day are listed as `(other)`. A referrer is recorded as its domain alone — never a full address, path or query — and a link from the site's own address is not counted. Owner only (API key); the platform admin may pass `owner`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of UTC days to include (default 30, clamp 1..365)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle of the account that owns the site (platform admin only; anyone else gets 404).

views.description: Views by people arriving from it

get.summary: Read the current site visitor session
get.description: Pages call it same-origin on the site's own address — its address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/` (only that site answers there), or its domain if it has one. Origin/Referer-gated. When the site has a connected domain and the call comes through another address, it returns signed_in false, sign_in_available false and code use_custom_domain with `domain` naming it, so the page can send the visitor to sign in there. Where sign-in is not offered (the legacy path address) the code is custom_domain_required. Checks the host, site and session expiry without extending the session. No CSRF header required. Anonymous visitors receive 200.

email.description: Latest verified OAuth identity email; users.username when no identity exists

provider.description: Google (more providers later); omitted when no OAuth identity exists

expires_at.description: Earlier of absolute and idle expiry (RFC3339)

domain.description: The site's bound custom domain; present only with code use_custom_domain

get.summary: Deprecated (Simple Host only): Read per-site JSON state
get.description: Deprecated compatibility API on Simple Host only. Existing behavior is retained. Simple Hack returns 410 legacy_storage_removed; use KV, SQLite or files there. Returns the JSON blob for this site (`null` if unset). PUBLIC store — no API key. A request with no `Origin` and no `Referer` (curl, an agent) is served as is; a request from a page (`Origin`/`Referer` set) is accepted only from the site's own page (`https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/`, or its domain). The site owner's (or the operator's) `X-API-Key` reads it from any page and names the owner's own site (how the owner app shows saved data). The response carries an `ETag`; send `If-None-Match: <etag>` to get a `304` when nothing changed (cheap polling). Never store secrets here.

put.summary: Deprecated (Simple Host only): Replace per-site JSON state
put.description: Deprecated compatibility API on Simple Host only. Existing behavior is retained. Simple Hack returns 410 legacy_storage_removed; use KV, SQLite or files there. Overwrites the whole blob (≤ 1 MB), last-write-wins. The document from before is kept for 30 days (GET .../state/history; restore with POST .../state/history/{id}/restore). Optionally pass `If-Match: <etag>` for optimistic concurrency (returns 412 on conflict). Origin-gated. Every save from a page needs a signed-in visitor: a visitor session (`X-SH-CSRF: 1`) on the site's own address — its address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/` (same-origin `/v1/sites/{sitename}/...`; only that site answers there), or its domain if it has one. Agents write with the site owner's `X-API-Key` (or the connector signed in as the owner; the platform admin's key writes any site) through the apex `https://simple-host.app/v1/...`, with no `Origin` (none is needed); another account's key gets 404 `{"error":"site not found"}` and writes nothing. A site with a connected domain takes page writes only there; writes through its other addresses answer 401 use_custom_domain. WRITE_AUTH_MODE=log/off and allow_anonymous_writes retain their compatibility exceptions. Invalid keys return 401 with {error: "invalid API key", code: "invalid_api_key"}.

Reads stay public. Never returned for a site that has no domain.

put.summary: Deprecated (Simple Host only): Declare what a data name is (owner)
put.description: Deprecated compatibility API on Simple Host only. Existing behavior is retained. Simple Hack returns 410 legacy_storage_removed; use KV, SQLite or files there. Owner only (X-API-Key, connector token, or the operator). Every piece of saved data has a name and one kind, and the kind decides who reads and who changes what. `{"kind": "content"}` is **Page info**: one JSON object only the owner writes (PUT .../data/{coll}) and anyone reads; a site declares at most 20 Page info names (SAVED_DATA_CONTENT_NAMES_MAX, 409 too_many_names); a name holding several entries cannot become one (409 has_entries). `{"kind": "entries"}` is **Submissions**: things visitors send. Options: `visibility` (`owner`, the default: only the owner reads them all, each visitor reads their own; or `public`: anyone reads them, without who sent them), `one_per_person` (one live entry per signed-in visitor), `notify` (email the owner: `daily`, the default while private; `each`, batched soon after they arrive; `off`, the default when public). A field left out keeps what the name had. A name nobody declared is **Shared** (anyone reads it, anyone signed in adds to it); with SAVED_DATA_DEFAULT_KIND=declare_first, on a site made after the kinds it takes no saves at all (409 declare_first). Product words are accepted for kind ("Page info", "Submissions"). Submissions need the site on an address of its own, where visitors sign in (409 custom_domain_required on instances without one); a site declares at most 50 Submissions names (SAVED_DATA_ENTRIES_NAMES_MAX, 409 too_many_names). Declaring a private name that holds entries as public Submissions would let anyone read them: 409 confirm_public (with `count`) until the request carries `"confirm_public": true`. A private name becomes Page info only while it is empty (409 has_entries). Both count what is in the name's Recently deleted too (a restore brings it back) and are checked under the name's lock. Public Submissions are refused on an install with WRITE_AUTH_MODE=off (409 visitor_sign_in_off). `{"kind": "mine"}` is **Personal**: one private record per signed-in visitor (a habit tracker, saved progress), stored private. Simple Host's owner tools (key, connector, owner app, exports) never show a person's record: the owner sees how many people have one and their size (from 3 people up). The site's own pages run in the visitor's browser and can read that visitor's record, so Personal is as private as the site's pages are trustworthy. A name holds records for at most 1,000 people (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_PEOPLE_MAX; a new person past it: 409 people_full). A name must be empty (nothing live or in Recently deleted) to become Personal (409 has_entries), and a Personal name that holds records never becomes another kind (409 has_records; both checked under the name's lock, so no save lands in between); a site declares at most 20 Personal names (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_NAMES_MAX). `{"kind": "board"}` is a **Shared board**: anyone reads it; signed-in visitors add, change and delete items one at a time; only the owner clears it; private entries become a board only with `confirm_public`; a site declares at most 20 Shared board names (SAVED_DATA_BOARD_NAMES_MAX). Neither takes options (400 invalid_kind), and both need the site's own address (409 custom_domain_required). Product words are accepted ("Personal", "Shared board").

post.description: Deprecated compatibility API on Simple Host only. Existing behavior is retained. Simple Hack returns 410 legacy_storage_removed; use KV, SQLite or files there. The same as POST .../collections/{coll} (same sign-in, Origin, privacy, `Idempotency-Key` and per-address rules), with the name's kind applied: Each new entry is at most 16 KB (SAVED_DATA_ENTRY_MAX_KB, 413 item_too_large); a name holds at most 10,000 live entries (SAVED_DATA_ENTRIES_MAX, 409 list_full); `one_per_person` refuses a second live entry from one visitor (409 one_per_person, with `id` of the entry they have; a visitor is the account, and its address with any +tag, so an entry from another account of the same address answers without `id`). Declared Submissions take entries only from a signed-in visitor (401 visitor_auth_required), never anonymously. Page info takes no entries (409 wrong_kind). An undeclared name is Shared and takes what the list route takes; where the install requires declaring first, nothing (409 declare_first). The site's who-may-save setting applies to every visitor (403 not_allowed_to_save; a block also matches the address with its +tag dropped); the owner always may. put.description: Deprecated compatibility API on Simple Host only. Existing behavior is retained. Simple Hack returns 410 legacy_storage_removed; use KV, SQLite or files there. post.summary: Give this site a nicer address (free <name>.simple-host.app or a custom domain)
post.description:
Optional. Every site already lives at its own address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/`, with sign-in and private lists. This gives it a nicer address; the site moves there and its old address redirects. A free address: send `{"domain": "<name>.simple-host.app"}` (one DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end, up to 63 characters). It is active at once with no DNS step — the answer has `status: active` and `verified_at`, and no `dns`. First come, first served: 409 domain_taken if another site holds it or it is already someone's handle (handles and free names share one namespace); reserved names (www, sites, api, admin, mail, cname and the platform's own hosts) get 400 name_reserved; anything else malformed gets 400 invalid_name. Once claimed it behaves exactly like a custom domain: the site is served at its root with a same-origin /v1 API and visitor sign-in, its person-address URL 302s there, and private collections take submissions there. A site has one own address: claiming one replaces a custom domain and vice versa. A free name the site lets go (switching, DELETE, or deleting the site) stays with it: it redirects to the site's current address and nobody else can claim it. A custom domain: bind ONE domain to the site (status starts as `pending`). Returns the two DNS records the owner must create: `dns` (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex) and `dns_txt`, the ownership record (TXT `_simple-host.<domain>` holding this site's token), which proves the domain is theirs and must stay in place. Nothing is verified or certified without it. A name another site on this server already serves is refused by the certificate issuer (failed, "already served here"). Once both records are seen, its certificate is requested automatically (at most 5 new domain certificates per account per day) (`certificate_status`: pending → issuing → live, or failed with the reason in `last_error`, retried) and the domain is served at its root, usually within minutes. If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. The platform's own zones (including event domains such as simple-hack.app) are refused (400 invalid_domain). A domain under the account's own address family may be connected; the exact domain wins. `*.<domain>` answers 400 use_address_family (see POST /v1/me/address-families). Owner only (API key).

www and the bare domain (where the certificate issuer runs, as on simple-host.app; absent elsewhere): binding `example.com` also sets up `www.example.com` (and binding `www.example.com` sets up `example.com`) as a redirect-only host that forwards (301) to the name chosen. The answer names it (`partner_domain`) with the record it needs (`dns_partner`); the TXT record on the chosen name covers both. It goes on the same certificate only if it points here and no other site on this server answers it; otherwise the chosen name goes live alone and `partner_status` is `not_set_up` with `partner_note` saying why.

post.summary: Connect *.<domain> so every site of the account answers under it
post.description:
An address family: the account connects `*.<suffix>` once (e.g. `*.trips.example.com`), and every site of the account named `<site_prefix><label>` then answers at `https://<label>.<suffix>/`, including sites created later. `site_prefix` is optional (with `voucher-`, `meera.voucher.example.com` is the site `voucher-meera`). All the account's matching sites answer; another account's sites never do. The label is one DNS label; names in ADDRESS_FAMILY_RESERVED_LABELS (default `www`) never name a site.

Two DNS records prove it: the wildcard record `dns` (CNAME `*.<suffix>` to the CNAME target; `dns_a` is the A-record alternative) and the ownership record `dns_txt` (TXT `_simple-host.<suffix>` holding the family's token, kept in place). Nothing is served before both are seen. A pending family expires after 24 hours (ADDRESS_FAMILY_UNPROVEN_HOURS). Several accounts may wait on the same name: the first to prove it wins, and the others are dropped and emailed. Once verified the family is exclusive: no other account can connect it, a family overlapping it, or a custom domain under it (409 domain_taken). The same account may put a custom domain under its own family; the exact domain wins.

Certificates: the operator sets up a wildcard certificate for `*.<suffix>` (`cert_mode` `wildcard`, the only mode now). Until then `certificate.status` is `waiting_for_operator` and nothing is served; write to support@simple-host.app. `per_host` (a certificate per site name) is not available yet (400 cert_mode_unavailable).

Main address (`canonical`, default true): a site's main address is its custom domain or free name, else its most specific canonical family address (longest site_prefix, then lowest rank, then suffix), else its own address. When a family address is the main one, the site's own address redirects there (302) and sign-in and saves happen there (the own address refuses writes with use_custom_domain). Every family address of a site keeps working either way. `canonical: false` keeps the site's own address as the main one.

A verified family that fails its checks (the TXT record gone, the wildcard moved) is emailed about after 24 hours and disconnected after 72; connecting it again needs the TXT record again. Answers 200 with the existing family when the account already has it. Owner only (API key).

What a cleanup run would do now, whether or not IDLE_CLEANUP is on: sites that would be warned (no visits by people and no new version for 90 days) and sites that would move to Recently deleted (warned 30 days ago with nothing done since). Sites taken offline by their owner, marked Keep, with their own domain or name, taken down, preview sites and admin sites are never listed. At most 500 of each. Nothing runs while `visit_data_ok` is false (under 90 days of visit records, or an analytics ingester that has not run for two days).

get.summary: The saved-data watch (admin)
get.description: Admin-only (403 for anyone else). Per site and summed over the last `days` days (default SAVED_DATA_WATCH_DAYS, 7; at most 90): how often each saved-data use that a later step makes owner-only or bounded happened, before anything is enforced. Counts only, never content. Metrics: put_by_visitor (a whole-document replace not by the owner), put_not_object (a document replaced by something other than an object), visitor_op_<op> (visitor PATCH ops by type), visitor_inc_large (a visitor inc beyond SAVED_DATA_WATCH_INC_MAX, 10), new_list_name (a visitor started a list name never used on the site), item_large (a list item over SAVED_DATA_WATCH_ITEM_KB, 16 KB).

get.summary: Per-endpoint API call analytics with caller geo (admin)
get.description: Admin-only. Aggregated API traffic for the retention window: call counts for today and the trailing week, today's error count, distinct caller IPs, a per-route breakdown and a per-IP breakdown with geo. Served from small day-granular aggregate tables, so it is cheap to poll. Geo (`where`, `org`) is resolved on the server from a local copy of DB-IP Lite — no caller IP is sent to a geolocation service — and is blank when that database is not installed. "IP Geolocation by DB-IP" (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0. A signed-in non-admin gets 404, not 403 — same rule as /v1/admin/users, so the endpoint does not confirm it exists to anyone who may not use it.

get.summary: API calls, new accounts and new sites per day, with calls by country (admin)

Countries are ISO-3166 alpha-2 codes looked up on this server from a local DB-IP file when the call is counted; no address is stored with these counts. Calls from this server or with no known country are in unknown_country_calls. Read from day-granular aggregates and cached a minute. A signed-in non-admin gets 404.

SQLite main database bytes are counted after checkpoint; transient WAL is excluded. KV key bytes count too. put.description: Kind is immutable. Creation defaults are owner read/write, write_mode=full and inherited passcode. Omitting write_mode on update preserves the existing mode. On Simple Host hosted/small boxes, write_mode=add allows visitor creation only (Simple Hack rejects add/own); read=own requires sign-in and filters by server-recorded visitor ID, including lists. Own with visitor writes requires add mode; own inserts always require sign-in. Switching non-own SQLite to own requires empty application tables with visitor_id TEXT; populated databases are refused with visitor_id_required because earlier raw identities are untrusted. Existing own rows are preserved. New own tables get that column and an index through schema. Changing to anyone can expose data or allow anonymous writes.

put.summary: Set one JSON value under the resource write policy
put.description: Visitor add mode creates only a new key, enforced by PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; 409 key_exists on collision. Owner can replace. New keys are normalized to NFC; exact legacy names remain readable and deletable. Visitor writes use the site's own origin and X-SH-CSRF header; anonymous writes require write=anyone. Visitor writes are limited per site/IP and per site/visitor by RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_IP and RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_VISITOR (429); reads consume no write tokens. Writes wait SITE_STORAGE_WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_MS (default 2000) for the deploy lock before 503 storage_busy with Retry-After.

delete.summary: Remove one KV key under the resource write policy

get.summary: Read table rows with fixed server-built SQL
get.description: Own reads use WHERE visitor_id = ? with the stable site-session identity. Table and order columns are checked against real schema; values are bound. Default order is an unshadowed rowid alias ascending; ordinary rowid tables only. Cursor includes order value and rowid, bound on the next query with matching order/desc. Owner sees all. No visitor SQL accepted. HEAD is a read. Visitor tables are limited to 100 columns and the complete response to SITE_STORAGE_SQL_RESULT_MAX_BYTES; visitor queries time out after one second. Reads do not lock writes or deploys.

post.summary: Insert one table row with fixed server-built SQL
post.description: One JSON object of real column names and scalar values. The server builds INSERT OR ABORT with bound values; visitor-supplied primary keys and rowids are refused. SQLite assigns the IDs and RETURNING supplies the result. Visitor visitor_id is ignored and identity is filled from the site session when the column exists. Visitor created_at is stamped with UTC time when the column exists; a client value is ignored. In add-only own-read databases, declared SQLite foreign keys verify the referenced row exists and has the same visitor_id or a NULL/empty owner catalog identity, using an indexed lookup per reference inside the insert transaction. Missing and another visitor's parents both return 404 invalid_reference; the insert is rolled back. Optional references must be all NULL; partial composite NULLs are refused. connector.description: Per-person OAuth 2.1 (authorization code; PKCE S256 required for every self-registered client). On Simple Host, a REST-audience access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` acts as that person's X-API-Key. On hosted Simple Hack, new consent issues one personal `sites events` grant for all event roles. MCP `hack_select_team` stores a publishing team on that grant; each website call rechecks approved membership and uses a separate scoped team credential. Legacy `sites team:<uuid>` grants remain site-only. Event roles still control each operation. MCP-audience tokens work only on /mcp. Discovery at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server publishes the scopes available on this instance; events is offered only in hosted hack mode.

idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotencyKey.description: Any unique string per write (e.g. a random UUID). For a writer with an identity (the owner's key or connector, or a visitor signed in on the site) a retry with the same key and the same body on the same site and route is saved once, for 24 hours (SAVED_DATA_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS), and answered with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: an append with the item it made, a PATCH with the document as it is now and its ETag. The same key with a different body gets 409 idempotency_key_reused; while the first request is still running, 409 idempotency_in_progress; a failed request is not remembered. Writes made without signing in ignore the header. Longer than 255 characters: 400 invalid_idempotency_key.

code.description: A stable snake_case name for the refusal, present where one status has more than one meaning. site_exists (409: this account already has a site of that name), domain_taken (409: the address belongs to another site or person), invalid_name (400: not 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), name_reserved (400: reserved by the platform), invalid_domain (400: not a domain that can be connected), site_quota_reached (403), append_only (409: public list items cannot be edited; the owner may still delete them), custom_domain_required (409: the site needs its own address first), not_an_object (409: the saved value is not a JSON object), private_visitor_only and private_needs_own_domain (403), use_custom_domain and visitor_auth_required (401), missing_api_key, wrong_auth_header (sent Authorization instead of X-API-Key), invalid_api_key (unknown, revoked or signed-out key), key_expired (past the expiry chosen when it was minted) and key_expired_idle (unused too long, KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS) (401), deploy_only_key (403: a deploy-only key on a route it may not call), csrf_required (403), recently_deleted (409: the name belongs to a site in Recently deleted), site_not_deleted (409: restore of a live site), confirm_required (400), not_found (404, private collections; also a PUT deploy to a site the account does not have), site_not_found (404: no site of that name on this account, on versions, rollback and site settings), export_link_invalid (404: the download link expired or is not valid), site_suspended (403: the operator has taken the site down; changes and public reads of its data are refused until it is restored, `reason` says why), account_suspended (403: the operator has suspended this account; its keys, connected apps and sign-in are refused, `reason` says why), site_offline (403: the owner has taken the site offline; visitor saves are refused until it is back online, the owner's key still writes), preview_read_only (403: a save made from a page opened as a version preview), preview_unavailable (409: the site has no address of its own to preview on), site_locked (403: the site has a passcode and the request carries no unlock for this host, nor the owner's or admin's key), invalid_passcode (400), passcodes_not_enabled and passcode_needs_own_address (409: a passcode cannot be set on this server), no_passcode (409), invalid_request (400), use_address_family (400: a *.<domain> sent to a site's domain route), no_address_family (404), invalid_site_prefix, invalid_rank, invalid_cert_mode, cert_mode_unavailable (400), address_family_limit and address_families_unavailable (409), signup_unavailable_region (403: this server does not allow sign-in or sign-up from the signer's region, new account or existing; an API key is unaffected). New codes may be added.

A 404 for a site the account does not have names the call that creates it (a deploy: add ?create=1 to the PUT, or POST) or points at GET /v1/sites (everything else). Present only on some errors; the wording may change.
